PDRN Explained: The Main Ingredient in Our Face Serum
What PDRN is, where it comes from, and what it does in the PDRN Brightening Serum, a daily face serum made by Tava Labs.
PDRN Explained: The Main Ingredient in Our Face Serum
The main ingredient in our serum is PDRN, which stands for polydeoxyribonucleotide. This article explains what PDRN is in plain words.
What PDRN is

PDRN is an ingredient made from DNA and sourced from salmon. It has been used in Korean skincare and in clinics for years, and it is now used in daily serums in the West. In cosmetics it is used to support skin that looks firm, even in tone, and bright.
Why it anchors our formula
The PDRN Brightening Serum is a face serum you use every day, and PDRN is used with other ingredients that each do a specific job:
Acetyl hexapeptide-8
, a peptide linked to skin that looks smoother and firmer.
Sodium hyaluronate
, the salt form of hyaluronic acid. It draws water into the surface of the skin so skin looks full and hydrated.
Glycerin and sodium PCA
, ingredients that attract water and help skin hold moisture through the day.
Panthenol
, also called provitamin B5. It conditions skin and helps keep the serum gentle enough to use twice a day.
What PDRN is not

It is not a drug, not an injection, and not a promise of a specific result. In a cosmetic serum, PDRN supports the look of healthy and bright skin as part of a regular routine. Changes are gradual and build with regular use, which is why the serum is made to be used every day, twice a day, starting slowly and building up as the plan describes.

The serum contains one main ingredient, other ingredients that support it, and no ingredient without a clear purpose. You can read the full list of ingredients on our Ingredients page. The PDRN Brightening Serum is 1 fl oz, which is 30 ml. It costs $49 for one bottle or $39 a month on subscription.
